title: Shortcut Keys (Ctrl / Command)
drDigitalIntro:
Every computer has a special key that powers keyboard shortcuts.
• On Windows, Chromebook, and Linux it's called Ctrl (Control). On a Mac it's called Command.
• Both keys do the same job — you hold one down and click a letter to trigger a shortcut.
• For example: Ctrl+C (or Command+C) copies selected text. Ctrl+V (or Command+V) pastes it.
• Shortcut instructions are often written with a plus sign: Ctrl+C means "hold Ctrl and press C at the same time."
• These shortcuts work in almost every app, on every kind of computer — learning them saves a lot of time.
drDigitalSuccess: That is the shortcut key. Whether yours says Ctrl or Command, it does the same job.
drDigitalHint: Find Ctrl in the bottom-left corner of your keyboard, or Command next to the space bar on Mac. Then click Continue.
